To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the circadian rhythms of C‐Fos expression in the suprachiasmastic nuclei of the common vole are distinct between the ventrolateral (v) and the dorsomedian (d) SCN.

in the common vole, the circadian organization is weak and that C‐FOS is expressed rhythmically in the dorsomedialis SCN under light/dark cycles and in a constitutive fashion under constant dim light.
C‐FOS rhythm in the dorsomedian part of the SCN in the common vole is weak or absent, whereas the ventrolateral part of the SCN shows a clear rhythm of C‐Fos expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparative approach to the circadian organization in the SCN of different rodent species.
circadian rhythms of the suprachiasmastic nuclei in the vole.
the circadian control of C‐Fos expression in the dorsomedialis and ventrolateral SCN of voles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in voles, the dorsomedial and the ventrolateral part of the SCN are differentially regulated.

in the common vole, c‐fos is a marker for circadian transcriptional activity in the dorsomedialis SCN but not the ventrolateralis SCN, and that the dorsomedialis and the ventrolateral nucleus are not coupled in their circadian transcriptional activities.

in the common vole, C‐FOS is expressed rhythmically in the ventrolaterally located part of the SCN under LD conditions, and that the dorsomedially located part of the master clock expresses c‐FOS constitutively under LD conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vole is a nocturnal rodent with weak circadian organization, and that the dorsomedial and ventrolateral SCN are differentially organized in the voles.
in voles, the dorsomedial and the ventrolateral regions of the SCN have different roles in the circadian clock.

in voles, the dorsomedial and ventrolateral SCN are distinct in terms of C‐Fos expression, and this is likely to reflect a different organization of the circadian clock in voles compared to other rodent species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the circadian clock in the SCN of the common vole is different from that in rodents that are more studied.
circadian rhythms of c‐Fos activity in the dorsomedially and the ventrolaterally located parts of the SCN are different in voles.
circadian rhythms in c‐FOS expression are not universal across rodent species.
